title: PBR Transmission Material (Transmission)
prompt:
Use Three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial to implement a scene containing 5 glass/transparent objects, supporting real-time adjustment of parameters including transmission, index of refraction (ior), thickness, and roughness, as well as object selection.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { RoomEnvironment } from 'three/addons/environments/RoomEnvironment.js';
</script>

[Scene]
(1) Exactly 5 objects: they may use different shapes such as spheres, tori, and icosahedra. All must use MeshPhysicalMaterial, with low metalness and transmission>0 to convey a glass-like appearance.
(2) Use PMREM + RoomEnvironment (or an equivalent environment map) to display transmission and reflections.
(3) id="objectSelect": <select> options correspond to the names of the 5 objects (consistent with their internal userData.name values or agreed-upon ids).
(4) id="transmissionSlider", id="iorSlider", id="thicknessSlider", id="roughnessSlider": type="range", with reasonable min/max/step values; changing a slider updates the corresponding material property of the currently selected object.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  selectedObject: string,   // Name or id of the currently selected object
  transmission: number,
  ior: number,
  thickness: number,
  roughness: number,
  objectCount: number       // Always 5
}

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
